1 · Knowledge graph

What is connected to what

Real data. Real computation. Real AI calls. Code builds this graph from 150 synthetic accounts-payable exceptions, the same sample the improvement loop runs on. It has 227 nodes and 637 edges: suppliers, exceptions, exception types, policies, controls and the people who decide.

Computed from the graph

  • 227 nodes
  • 637 edges
  • 1 connected component
  • 5.6 mean degree

Nodes by type

  • Control: 8
  • Exception: 150
  • Exception type: 6
  • Policy: 6
  • Role: 3
  • Supplier: 54

Most exceptions

  1. Supplier 38: 8
  2. Supplier 21: 6
  3. Supplier 57: 6
  4. Supplier 41: 5
  5. Supplier 46: 5

Highest risk score

  1. Supplier 34: 7 (3 need a person, 4 wrong agent suggestions)
  2. Supplier 38: 5 (2 need a person, 3 wrong agent suggestions)
  3. Supplier 32: 5 (2 need a person, 3 wrong agent suggestions)
  4. Supplier 41: 4 (2 need a person, 2 wrong agent suggestions)
  5. Supplier 56: 4 (2 need a person, 2 wrong agent suggestions)

Most connected nodes

  1. AP clerk (reviewer): degree 140
  2. Match tolerance 1%: degree 72
  3. Small-supplier protection: degree 46
  4. Price variance: degree 44
  5. Confidence floor 0.95: degree 34

Risk score = exceptions that need a person + exceptions where the resolver agent suggested the wrong resolution. Ties go to the larger total amount. Under the baseline policy, 1 exception go to the resolver agent, 138 to an AP clerk and 11 to a senior approver.

2 · Skill graph

Who may do what, and what stops them

Each agent on this site appears here with its skills, tools, data, controls and autonomy level. Limits come from the site’s own code: the action whitelist, the scorer lock, the do-not-automate list and the call budget. Pick an agent to see what it can and cannot do.

  • 78 nodes
  • 160 edges
  • 26 controls, all from the library
  • 9 agents
What each agent can and cannot do
AgentCan (autonomy level)Cannot (blocked by)
Proposer (AI)Propose policy variants (L1)Change the scorer, goal or test set (MR-10); Ship a one-way-door change (HO-06 SOD-03); Automate a bank-detail change (TAL-05 TAL-07); Loosen a guardrail cap (SOD-01); Write to the requests table (IAM-03); Exceed the model-call budget (CST-03 TAL-04)
Guardrail harness (code)Run a policy over the sample (L4); Check fitness rules and block (L4); Ship a two-way-door change (L3)Automate a bank-detail change (TAL-05 TAL-07)
Supervisor (AI)Explain results and draft decision cards (L1)Change the scorer, goal or test set (MR-10); Ship a one-way-door change (HO-06 SOD-03); Loosen a guardrail cap (SOD-01); Write to the requests table (IAM-03); Exceed the model-call budget (CST-03 TAL-04)
Evaluator (code)Score the goal number (L4)–
Archivist (code)Archive variants and lineage (L4)–
Room voices (AI)Answer room instructions (L1)Change the scorer, goal or test set (MR-10); Ship a one-way-door change (HO-06 SOD-03); Automate a bank-detail change (TAL-05 TAL-07); Loosen a guardrail cap (SOD-01); Take an action outside the whitelist (TAL-03 IAM-03); Write to the requests table (IAM-03); Exceed the model-call budget (CST-03 TAL-04)
Book guide (AI)Answer from the book (L1); Pass a consented lead to Hemanth (L1)Take an action outside the whitelist (TAL-03 IAM-03); Send a request without the visitor’s consent (HO-01 PRV-04); Exceed the model-call budget (CST-03 TAL-04)
Graph agent (AI)Answer from a code-selected subgraph (L1)Change the scorer, goal or test set (MR-10); Take an action outside the whitelist (TAL-03 IAM-03); Write to the requests table (IAM-03); Exceed the model-call budget (CST-03 TAL-04)

All 78 nodes of the skill graph, as a table
IDTypeLabelFacts
AG-proposerAgentProposer (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Proposes two policy variants per generation.; source: functions/api/loop/step.ts
AG-harnessAgentGuardrail harness (code)kind: Code; does: Runs each variant over the sample and checks the fitness rules.; source: lib/loop.ts
AG-supervisorAgentSupervisor (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Explains results and writes decision cards. Code decides the doors.; source: functions/api/loop/step.ts
AG-evaluatorAgentEvaluator (code)kind: Code; does: Computes the goal number with the locked scorer.; source: lib/loop.ts
AG-archivistAgentArchivist (code)kind: Code; does: Keeps every variant, its parent and its scores.; source: lib/loop.ts
AG-roomAgentRoom voices (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Answers visitor instructions in the operations room.; source: functions/api/agents.ts
AG-guideAgentBook guide (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Answers questions from the book knowledge pack.; source: functions/api/guide.ts
AG-graphAgentGraph agent (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Answers from a subgraph that code selected.; source: functions/api/graph/ask.ts
AG-intakeAgentIntake agent (AI)kind: AI agent; does: Asks short questions and fills a request card.; source: functions/api/intake.ts
SK-proposeSkillPropose policy variantsautonomy: L1; why: Suggests only. Code tests every variant and decides what ships.; controls: MR-10 PCS-02 TRC-05 CST-03
SK-runpolicySkillRun a policy over the sampleautonomy: L4; why: Deterministic code. It runs and reports every time.; controls: MR-01 TAL-05
SK-guardSkillCheck fitness rules and blockautonomy: L4; why: Blocks failing variants and any scorer change, in code.; controls: MR-10 SOD-02 SOD-01
SK-shipSkillShip a two-way-door changeautonomy: L3; why: Acts within limits, behind a one-click undo.; controls: TAL-02 TAL-06 TRC-01
SK-explainSkillExplain results and draft decision cardsautonomy: L1; why: Explains. A named person approves one-way doors.; controls: HO-01 HO-06 PCS-02 CST-03
SK-scoreSkillScore the goal numberautonomy: L4; why: Locked code outside the loop.; controls: MR-10 MR-09
SK-archiveSkillArchive variants and lineageautonomy: L4; why: Records every variant, parent and approver.; controls: TRC-05 TRC-04
SK-roomSkillAnswer room instructionsautonomy: L1; why: Talks and picks at most one whitelisted action: propose_variant, tighten_guardrail, request_decision, reframe_goal, none.; controls: TAL-03 PCS-01 PCS-03 TAL-04 CST-03
SK-guideSkillAnswer from the bookautonomy: L1; why: Answers only from the knowledge pack.; controls: MR-04 PCS-01 PCS-05 TAL-04
SK-leadSkillPass a consented lead to Hemanthautonomy: L1; why: Stores a lead only when the visitor submits it.; controls: PRV-01 PRV-04 TAL-04
SK-graphSkillAnswer from a code-selected subgraphautonomy: L1; why: Read only. Cited node IDs are checked in code.; controls: MR-04 PCS-01 PCS-02 CST-03 TAL-04
SK-intakeSkillFill a request card by conversationautonomy: L1; why: Asks and extracts only. Code checks every field.; controls: PCS-01 PCS-02 PRV-01 PRV-04 CST-03 TAL-04
SK-submitSkillStore a request the visitor confirmedautonomy: L1; why: Code stores it only after the visitor ticks consent and presses Send.; controls: HO-01 PRV-01 TAL-04
DENY-scorerCannot doCannot: Change the scorer, goal or test sethow: Any proposed key matching /scor|evaluat|metric|goal|grader|reward|test.?set|benchmark|measure|judge/i is blocked before it runs.; controls: MR-10
DENY-onewayCannot doCannot: Ship a one-way-door changehow: Code flags one-way doors (for example an auto-approve limit above $5,000) and sends them to a person.; controls: HO-06 SOD-03
DENY-bankCannot doCannot: Automate a bank-detail changehow: Hard-coded do-not-automate list: bank_detail_change. Not a setting.; controls: TAL-05 TAL-07
DENY-loosenCannot doCannot: Loosen a guardrail caphow: Caps can only tighten. Looser values are clamped in code.; controls: SOD-01
DENY-actionsCannot doCannot: Take an action outside the whitelisthow: Unknown action types become none. Extra fields are dropped.; controls: TAL-03 IAM-03
DENY-unconsentedCannot doCannot: Send a request without the visitor’s consenthow: The submit path refuses any request without explicit consent. The model cannot call it.; controls: HO-01 PRV-04
DENY-requestsCannot doCannot: Write to the requests tablehow: Only the guide and intake submit paths write requests, after the visitor confirms.; controls: IAM-03
DENY-budgetCannot doCannot: Exceed the model-call budgethow: Calls are counted in the rate-limit table: 120 per day site-wide.; controls: CST-03 TAL-04
TOOL-modelTool or APIModel gatewaywhat: One GPT-class model, with a smaller fallback model.
TOOL-loopTool or APIPOST /api/loop/stepwhat: Actions: decide, generation, reframe, start, why.
TOOL-agentsTool or APIPOST /api/agentswhat: Whitelisted actions: propose_variant, tighten_guardrail, request_decision, reframe_goal, none.
TOOL-guideTool or APIPOST /api/guidewhat: Chat and consented lead capture.
TOOL-graphTool or APIPOST /api/graph/askwhat: Graph traversal in code, then one model call.
TOOL-intakeTool or APIPOST /api/intakewhat: One model call per turn; submit only with consent.
TOOL-runnerTool or APIPolicy runnerwhat: Runs a policy over all sample exceptions. Deterministic.
TOOL-capsTool or APICall budgetwhat: 10 calls per loop run; 120 model calls per day, site-wide.
DATA-sampleDataSample AP exceptionswhat: 150 synthetic exceptions. Read only.
DATA-metricsDataAggregate resultswhat: Goal number and guardrail readings per variant.
DATA-policyDataPolicy configwhat: Six settings: auto_approve_limit, match_tolerance_pct, senior_review_above, small_supplier_protection, confidence_floor, audit_trace.
DATA-scorerDataLocked scorer and goalwhat: Outside the loop. No agent may edit it.
DATA-archiveDataVariant archivewhat: Kept in the visitor’s browser for the run.
DATA-knowledgeDataBook knowledge packwhat: The guide’s source text.
DATA-requestsDataRequests tablewhat: Leads a visitor submits with consent.
DATA-graphsDataKnowledge and skill graphswhat: Built from committed files at build time.
DATA-ratelimitsDataRate-limit tablewhat: Counts calls for the caps. No content.
CST-03ControlCST-03 Model quotasname: Model quotas; purpose: Set token and call quotas per agent at the model gateway.; required from: L1
HO-01ControlHO-01 Decision card for approvalsname: Decision card for approvals; purpose: Show the approver the proposal, evidence, rule, confidence and options on one card.; required from: L2
HO-06ControlHO-06 Named approval for one-way-door changesname: Named approval for one-way-door changes; purpose: A named person approves any change that is hard to undo before it ships.; required from: L1
IAM-03ControlIAM-03 Least-privilege tool scopesname: Least-privilege tool scopes; purpose: Give each agent only the read and write scopes that its step needs.; required from: L1
MR-01ControlMR-01 Pre-release evaluation suitename: Pre-release evaluation suite; purpose: Test each agent and model version against a fixed set of evaluations before release.; required from: L1
MR-04ControlMR-04 Groundedness and citation checkname: Groundedness and citation check; purpose: Check that each claim in an agent output cites a retrieved source.; required from: L1
MR-09ControlMR-09 Shadow run before promotionname: Shadow run before promotion; purpose: Run a new agent version beside people, with no effect, before it gains a level.; required from: L2
MR-10ControlMR-10 Scorer isolation for improvement loopsname: Scorer isolation for improvement loops; purpose: An improvement loop may never change the scorer, the test set or the guardrails that judge it.; required from: L1
PCS-01ControlPCS-01 Untrusted content is dataname: Untrusted content is data; purpose: Treat emails, documents, web pages and transcripts as data. Never treat them as instructions.; required from: L1
PCS-02ControlPCS-02 Output schema validationname: Output schema validation; purpose: Accept agent output only when it matches the expected schema and value ranges.; required from: L1
PCS-03ControlPCS-03 No secrets or limits in promptsname: No secrets or limits in prompts; purpose: Keep secrets, keys and limits out of prompts. Detect attempts to extract the system instructions.; required from: L1
PCS-05ControlPCS-05 Content safety filtername: Content safety filter; purpose: Screen inputs and outputs for harmful, offensive or off-policy content.; required from: L1
PRV-01ControlPRV-01 Data minimization in contextname: Data minimization in context; purpose: Only the fields that a step needs enter the model context.; required from: L1
PRV-04ControlPRV-04 Agent disclosure and recording noticename: Agent disclosure and recording notice; purpose: Tell people that they deal with an agent, and tell callers when a call is recorded.; required from: L1
SOD-01ControlSOD-01 Approver cannot change limitsname: Approver cannot change limits; purpose: The person who approves agent actions may not change the limits, instructions or tools of that agent.; required from: L2
SOD-02ControlSOD-02 Maker-checker for agent changesname: Maker-checker for agent changes; purpose: One person cannot both change an agent and release that change.; required from: L1
SOD-03ControlSOD-03 Agent cannot approve its own proposalname: Agent cannot approve its own proposal; purpose: The agent that proposes an action cannot approve or commit that action.; required from: L2
TAL-02ControlTAL-02 Propose, validate, route, commitname: Propose, validate, route, commit; purpose: The agent proposes. Deterministic rules validate, route and commit.; required from: L3
TAL-03ControlTAL-03 Typed tool contractsname: Typed tool contracts; purpose: Agents call only registered tools with typed inputs, typed outputs and declared scopes.; required from: L1
TAL-04ControlTAL-04 Rate and volume limitsname: Rate and volume limits; purpose: Cap the actions per minute and per day for each agent and each tool.; required from: L2
TAL-05ControlTAL-05 Do-not-automate listname: Do-not-automate list; purpose: Named decisions stay with people. Agents cannot hold the permissions for those decisions.; required from: L0
TAL-06ControlTAL-06 Idempotent commit and reversal pathname: Idempotent commit and reversal path; purpose: Every committed action has a tested reversal. No action can post twice.; required from: L3
TAL-07ControlTAL-07 Out-of-band verification for bank changesname: Out-of-band verification for bank changes; purpose: A person verifies each bank-detail change by calling a known number from the master record.; required from: L0
TRC-01ControlTRC-01 Decision trace before commitname: Decision trace before commit; purpose: Write what the agent saw, decided and did before any action commits.; required from: L1
TRC-04ControlTRC-04 Change log for agentsname: Change log for agents; purpose: Log every change to instructions, tools, limits and model versions.; required from: L1
TRC-05ControlTRC-05 Variant lineage and archivename: Variant lineage and archive; purpose: Keep every variant an improvement loop proposed, with its parent, change, scores and decision.; required from: L1

3 · Enterprise brain

The layer that connects graphs, models and memory

Ask a question. Code routes it, walks the graphs and picks a model family. One real model call answers from the subgraph only. Code checks the answer. The trace joins your session memory, and the map grows.

  1. Signal. Your question arrives on the web. Chat, email, voice, IoT and robot signals are not connected in this demo.
  2. Brain router. 10 rules in code read the question and pick the graph and the model family.
  3. Graph lookup. Code walks the knowledge graph or the skill graph and selects a subgraph.
  4. Model family. One GPT-class model call writes the answer. Every other family is routed to, not run in this demo. What each family does and where it fits.
  5. Skill and agent. The graph agent answers from the subgraph only.
  6. Gate. Code checks citations, vendor names, prompt leaks, length and the call budget: MR-04 PCS-01 PCS-02 PCS-05 CST-03 TAL-04 TRC-01 RES-02.
  7. Action. A read-only answer with cited nodes.
  8. Trace and memory. The trace is added to your session memory in this browser tab. Nothing is stored on the server.

Limits and what is real

Real. The graphs, the routing, the traversal and every check are code. The answer is one call to a GPT-class model, with a smaller model as fallback.

Not run. Other model families appear on the map so you see the choice. The demo labels them “routed to, not run in this demo” and shows no output for them. See what each family does and where it fits.

Limits. Eight questions per visitor per hour. The site shares a daily allowance of model calls that resets at midnight UTC. Your questions are not stored.

Related: the graph-grounded agent pattern and controls MR-04 PCS-01 MR-10.
